fieldsRead.text: The English-taught Arts and Culture Studies specialisation examines visual art, literature, music, film, television and performance through historical, theoretical and social perspectives. Students develop cultural criticism, research and cultural-sector practice.

Three UCR programmes offer related routes through arts and media, culture and power, or literature and communication. Radboud provides dedicated music study, festival production and a separate bachelor thesis. This comparison uses Radboud’s published indicative plan for students starting in 2027.
Arts and Culture Studies — standard domestic pathway

This indicative entrant plan begins in 2027–2028 and continues through 2029–2030. Radboud labels its future offerings provisional and subject to change. The plan preserves two 15-EC Faculty of Arts minors and 30 EC of free electives; it does not guarantee future courses or replace the applicable programme regulations.
Two 15-EC Faculty of Arts minors, one per second-year semester; this is structured choice space, not unrestricted electives.
Required 10-EC bachelor thesis; current published progression requires completion of compulsory second-year major courses. Future regulations may change.

30 EC free-choice space. In the standard domestic pathway, 15 EC is taken in each semester; courses, internship and study abroad are possibilities subject to programme rules. The alternative exchange pathway is not added.

Mentoring/PPO and the RADAr academic-language requirement carry 0 EC and are separate from the 180-EC total. The programme currently requires attendance, including mentoring, and 45 first-year EC for positive study advice, subject to personal circumstances.
Both introduce close visual analysis and interpretation of artworks in historical context.

Partial cultural-repertoire relationship through Renaissance Italian visual art and its Mediterranean, Asian, African and American connections. UCR concentrates on this historical artistic period rather than Radboud’s wider European/global cultural repertoire.
Both examine visual culture and the institutions that shape modern artistic meaning; UCR focuses specifically on modern art and museums.

Required 10-EC independent bachelor thesis. Scheduled UCR historical and subject-specific research develops source analysis and papers; it does not replace this degree requirement. Optional independent research is separate from the scheduled 180 EC.

Arts and Culture Studies at Radboud University
New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

The UCR programmes offer substantial art history, literature, film, media and cultural interpretation. Radboud additionally requires dedicated music analysis and music as technology, festival work and a separate bachelor thesis. UCR creative communication and subject-specific research offer different forms of practice and inquiry; they do not reproduce these specialist requirements.

A broad arts-and-culture route combining art history and heritage, literature, film and media with stylistics, social theory, ethics and qualitative inquiry. Historiography examines how art is interpreted; historical research develops source criticism and a substantial paper, rather than replacing a required cultural-studies thesis.

A cultural-studies route examining identity and power through art, literature, media, gender history and heritage. Political philosophy, social theory, empire, social movements and conflict provide specific contexts; qualitative inquiry and historical research develop complementary methods.

A literature, film and communication route organised around close reading, adaptation, documentary, rhetoric, stylistics and creative communication. Art history and material culture provide selected cultural contexts; general philosophy, ethics and qualitative methods contribute complementary analytical tools.
